name: Postharvest Cold & Ambient Sorting
description: Sort incoming postharvest flower and foliage shipments into appropriate environmental storage areas to maximize vase life and prevent chilling injury or toxic sap cross-contamination. Cold-tolerant temperate cut flowers and hardy greens are routed to a standard Floral Cooler held at 2°C–4°C, chilling-sensitive tropical blooms to an Ambient Tropical Bench maintained at 13°C–18°C, and sap-exuding Narcissus varieties to dedicated Narcissus Isolation Vessels for conditioning.

steps: Identify incoming temperate cut flowers and foliage (Eucalyptus Foliage Bunches, Dutch White Lilies [Lilium orientalis], and Freedom Red Roses [Rosa]) and store them immediately in the Floral Cooler set to 2°C–4°C.
Identify chilling-sensitive tropical blooms (Anthurium Blooms and Vanda Orchids) and place them on the Ambient Tropical Bench held at 13°C–18°C, never permitting exposure below 10°C.

Identify Narcissus species (Fresh-cut Golden Daffodils and Paperwhite Jonquils [Narcissus tazetta]) and isolate them in dedicated Narcissus Isolation Vessels filled with fresh water for a minimum of 12 hours before considering cross-flower arrangement.
Keep ambient tropicals away from refrigerated drafts and cold chamber shelving to avoid irreversible black chilling spots and petal drop.
Prevent water sharing between isolated Narcissus containers and buckets containing other flower types to stop toxic lycorine alkaloid sap transmission.
caveats: Narcissus species exude toxic mucilage containing lycorine alkaloid that clogs vascular systems and poisons companion flowers; never mix them in communal buckets without proper isolated conditioning.

Tropical flowers such as Anthuriums and Vanda Orchids suffer rapid chilling necrosis, floret drop, and black spotting when exposed to temperatures below 10°C; do not place them inside standard refrigerated floral coolers.
Temperate flowers like roses and lilies held in warm ambient storage open prematurely and experience drastic reductions in vase life due to elevated respiration rates.
Hardy cut foliage like eucalyptus desiccates or loses dormancy if kept out of cold-chain refrigeration.
